title: Physically Typed and Geometry-Aware Representations for Earth Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.13868v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Earth-observation (EO) foundation models have become exceptionally effective at learning se mantic, high-dimensional geospatial embeddings, while modern weather and climate models have demonstrated that Earth-specific geometry, spherical operators, meshes, and hybrid physical solvers can materially improve prediction. Yet these two advances are not equivalent. A conventional latent embedding has no inherent physical transformation law, whereas scalar fields, tangent polar-vector fields, axial/pseudovector quantities, covectors, and higher-order tensors transform differently under rotations, reflections, and changes of local coordinate frame. This proposal asks whether a general purpose Earth foundation model should preserve those distinctions explicitly, or whether standard embeddings plus augmentation already learn everything that matters. translated_title: 地球基础模型的物理类型化与几何感知表示
translated_abstract: 地球观测（EO）基础模型在学习语义化、高维地理空间嵌入表示方面已变得极为有效，而现代天气和气候模型则已证明，地球特有的几何结构、球面算子、网格以及混合物理求解器能够显著提升预测性能。然而，这两项进展并不等价。传统的潜在嵌入表示不具备内在的物理变换规律，而标量场、切向极向量场、轴向量/赝向量量、余向量以及高阶张量在旋转、反射和局部坐标系变换下的变换方式各不相同。本提案探讨的核心问题是：通用地球基础模型是否应当显式地保留这些物理区分，还是标准的嵌入表示加数据增广已足以学习所有重要的信息。因此，其核心贡献并非理所当然地采用更复杂的架构，而是一种……
tldr: 该论文提出通用地球基础模型应显式保留物理类型化与几何感知的表示，尊重标量场、向量场、张量等物理量在旋转、反射等变换下的不同规律，而非仅依赖标准潜在嵌入加数据增广。
